The aggregate properties of such a composite would represent a step-fold innovation in electrocaloric technology that would fundamentally alter the product mapping of many aerospace residential, commercial and automotive systems. Moreover, the technology would enable the emergence of new cooling systems for portable, supplemental, and critical need cooling. We focus our efforts on ferroelectric behavior in cyano biphenyl LC mesogens, which have shown promise as electrocaloric materials. These materials possess the attributes of a high density of dipole moieties, the order of which can be directly influenced by an external electric field, and good resistance to dielectric breakdown. Further, the order-disorder transition behavior represents a large change in entropy yielding the potential for a large magnitude electrocaloric effect. The technology innovation used in this effort to realize a step-change improvement in solid state electrocaloric materials is to combine the superior electrocaloric properties of liquid crystal (LC) mesogens with the excellent electrical properties, mechanical properties, and useful form factor of a thin polymer film produced through a scalable additive manufacturing technique. This technique is based on electrospray processing which enables tunable film features such as thickness and roughness. Background Heating, venting, and air conditioning systems (HVAC) account for nearly 30% of the total energy use in the United States, some 14 Quads of energy per year (14x1015 BTU’s/year) with an attendant 3x108 tons of annual carbon emissions. Concomitantly, there is explosive growth for HVAC systems in emerging markets https://www.renewaire.com/wp- content/uploads/2018/09/White-Paper_HVAC-Trends_Final2.pdf with a total global energy consumption expected for HVAC systems of approximately $207B/yr by 2022. The sale and installation of vapor compression (VC) based cooling systems outranks all other modes of cooling due to low cost, dependability, and efficiency. However, the continued proliferation of traditional VC systems raises two concerns: (1) The prospect of a significant rise in the release of refrigerants with high global warming potential (GWP) either through faulty assembly or when servicing.
